summary: Andaman and Nicobar - As per the Andaman and Nicobar startup policy, the UT Administration, through Andaman and Nicobar Islands Integrated Development Corporation Limited (ANIIDCO Ltd), would create an initial innovation fund of INR 1 crore to support the establishment of startup incubators. Capital from the fund corpus will also be utilised to develop coworking spaces in the region.

Assam – As per the Assam startup policy, the state government proposed to provide a maximum of @75% grant subject to a limit of a maximum of INR 5 crore for the establishment of incubation centres at IIT, Engineering colleges, Universities, Biotechnology parks, IT Park, Educational institutions.

Andhra Pradesh– As per the Andhra Pradesh startup policy, host Institutes of TBIs that are recognised by the National Science and Technology Entrepreneurship Development Board (NSTEDB) shall be entitled to a lease of land and space for a period of 90 years for setting up TBIs and related infrastructure to create world-class live-work-Play environments at Government-owned IT parks.

Bihar – As per the Bihar startup policy, the state government would provide fiscal grant to state supported Incubators @3%of the investment received by its incubatees from SEBI registered AIFs (Alternate Investment Funds) or grant received from Government of India for promoting technology based (IPR)startups and @5% for startups in social sectors providing solutions to public service access problems in Bihar in areas like health, education and nutrition etc. The Government shall provide financial assistance to match the funding raised by Incubator(s) from Government of India and Multilateral donor agencies on 1:1 basis on same terms and conditions.

Chhattisgarh– As per the Chhattisgarh startup policy, an Innovation Fund would be created for setting up the core Incubator-cum Accelerator for at least three years. The fund will be used for setting up infrastructure and office space, bearing operating expenditure, organising international, national, and local events, etc.

Goa – All educational institutes in Goa, affiliated with a recognised public university, can avail of a one-time grant of up to INR 10 lakhs towards capital expenses for setting up an incubator within their institute campuses for the purpose of nurturing start-ups founded by students enrolled in these institutes.

Gujarat – The incubators have a choice between Gujarat State Startup Policy or Industries and Mines department. Eligible incubators will be provided one-time capital assistance at the rate of 50% of Gross Fixed Capital Investment and many other incentives.
Haryana – The state startup policy aims to establish at least 22 Technology Business Incubators and Accelerators across different sectors of Haryana.

Himachal Pradesh– As per the Himachal Pradesh startup policy, financial assistance will be provided for three years to the selected institutions for setting up the incubator and other activities. The maximum financial assistance will be provided @ INR 30 lakhs per incubator per year up to a period of three years.

Jharkhand– As per the Jharkhand startup policy, the government funded reputed and prestigious institutes of Jharkhand would be provided with a sum of INR 50 lakhs annually for the first 5 years for setting up incubation/innovation centres.

Karnataka– As per the Karnataka startup policy, the state support would provide initial capital costs for equipment and facilities and recurring costs of management of TBI for a three-year period, extendable by another two years based on performance, at the end of which the incubators are expected to become self-sufficient.

Madhya Pradesh– As per the Madhya Pradesh startup policy, eligible host Institutions shall be provided a capital grant of max 50% for fixed-cost investment for setting up an incubator, subject to a maximum of INR 50 lakhs by the Madhya Pradesh government.

Maharashtra– As per the Maharashtra startup policy, the Maharashtra state would institute an Infrastructure Fund to provide assistance to incubators, accelerators, CoEs, and tinkering labs to cover capital and operational expenditures in the establishment and/or expansion of facilities.

Manipur – As per the Manipur startup policy, the state would provide special fiscal incentive to incubators @2% of the investment received by its incubates from SEBI registered Venture Capital/Private Equity into Manipur based startups.
Nagaland – As per the Nagaland startup policy, the state government shall provide financial assistance up to INR 25 Lakhs as capital grant to the incubators.

Odisha– As per the Odisha startup policy, approved educational institutions will be eligible for a one time grant of 50% of capital cost (excluding the cost of the building) up to a maximum of INR 1 Crore to setup incubator facility by the Odisha state government.

Puducherry– As per the Puducherry startup policy, the state government shall allot land or built up space to the startup cell in the Industrial Estates/IT Parks depending on the availability on preferential basis for establishment of Incubators/ Accelerator, Co-working space, Fab Lab, etc.
Punjab – As per the Punjab startup policy, host institutes would be offered with a capital grant of 100% of FCI subject to a maximum of INR 1 Crore for setting up Incubators.

Rajasthan– A one time gant for capital items will be given to host institutes by the Rajasthan state government for the purpose of entrepreneurship development and startup events in the region, with a maximum of INR 50 lakhs.

Tamil Nadu– As per the Tamil Nadu startup policy, the state Government would allot land at nominal lease for duration of 99 years to establish ‘Startup Parks’ at appropriate places by entrepreneurs/Startups including NRIs from Tamil Diaspora.
Telangana – As per the Telangana startup policy, the state government would match the funding raised by the Incubator from Government of India on a 1:1 basis as matching grants.

Uttar Pradesh– As per the UP startup policy host Institutes shall be provided capital grant of max 50% for IT infrastructure setup, subject to maximum of INR 25 lakhs. The same limit shall be granted for strengthening existing Incubators in case of expansion subject to the capacity utilisation of the existing Incubator for 2 years by the UP state government.

Uttarakhand– As per the Uttarakhand startup policy, host institutes shall be provided capital grant of maximum 50% for IT Infrastructure setup, subject to maximum of INR 25 lakhs capital grant of 50% of the capital cost up to a maximum of INR 1 Crore will be provided to incubators.
West Bengal– As per the West Bengal startup policy, state would provide INR 10 Lakhs to Universities in the state to create a central Entrepreneurship Development Centre (EDC).

Source description: Raido is a 360° mobility platform built to make everyday travel simple, affordable, and fair for drivers. In short — Raido connects customers with drivers on a zero-commission model. Customers don’t pay extra per ride. Instead, drivers use Raido through a small ₹25/day subscription, so they keep almost all their earnings. Here’s what Raido offers: Taxi / Ride services – affordable local rides Raido School – subscription-based school commute with pickup/drop, live tracking, and parent notifications Driver-first platform – no heavy commissions, more income for drivers Currently operational in Hosur and Chennai It’s designed as a licensed and regulated mobility ecosystem, aiming to cover end-to-end transport needs (360° mobility).

Organisation listed in the public VISTAS Incubation Centre incubatee table. Source description: SPLLIT is a passenger-to-passenger shared mobility platform designed to make daily commuting affordable, efficient, and trustworthy for students and young professionals. Many commuters travel the same routes at the same time but lack a reliable way to connect with each other. Existing ride-hailing platforms are driver-centric, while informal solutions like WhatsApp groups are unsafe and inconsistent. SPLLIT solves this problem using AI-based route and time matching that connects verified users traveling similar routes. Users pay a low ₹19 daily connection fee to unlock matched rides, communicate through in-app chat or calls, and split travel costs among themselves. A feedback-driven trust system with ID verification and ratings improves safety and reliability. The platform follows a campus-first approach, starting with IIT Madras and similar environments to ensure high match density and fast adoption. In the long term, SPLLIT aims to expand into tech parks, co-living spaces, event travel, and subscription-based group mobility solutions, reducing commuting costs, traffic congestion, and environmental impact.

Our products are currently exported to markets including Ireland, Australia, Maldives, Canada, the UK, and the USA. Backed by modern processing facilities and strict quality control systems, we ensure consistent taste, nutrition, and compliance across all batches. Alongside our B2B operations, we own and develop our in-house consumer brand Ashwatham – Full of Goodness, which promotes clean-label, nutrient-rich foods rooted in India’s traditional agricultural wisdom. Our portfolio includes millet flours, traditional rice, health mixes, and functional food innovations such as moringa-based products. Driven by the mission to make Indian superfoods globally accessible, B Signature bridges farmers, technology, and global markets to deliver wholesome, authentic, and sustainable food solutions.

Organisation listed in the public VISTAS Incubation Centre incubatee table. Source description: Founder Edge is an on-demand platform built to help startup founders make better decisions, faster. It connects founders with experienced operators—people who have already built, scaled, and solved real startup challenges—through 1:1 paid video sessions. Instead of spending weeks figuring things out alone or relying on generic advice, founders can directly speak to someone who has faced a similar problem and get clear, actionable guidance. Unlike traditional mentorship, which is often long-term, unstructured, and dependent on access or networks, Founder Edge is designed for instant, problem-specific support. Founders don’t need to join cohorts, wait for introductions, or sit through generic sessions. They can find the right expert, book a session, and get exactly what they need—when they need it. The platform focuses on areas like go-to-market strategy, growth, product, hiring, and fundraising, ensuring founders receive practical insights, not theory. It removes guesswork and replaces it with clarity, speed, and execution. Looking ahead, Founder Edge will integrate AI to enhance expert matching, provide pre-session insights, and deliver post-session action plans. The long-term vision includes building a global expert network and attracting strategic investors to scale access, improve product capabilities, and become the default platform for on-demand startup expertise.

The official portfolio page states that C-CAMP has interacted with over 500 inventors and entrepreneurs and supported over 100 start-ups/spin-offs through funding, bio-incubation and mentorship.
The institutional page lists seed funding schemes for startups as part of C-CAMP’s entrepreneurship and innovation mandate.
The institutional page lists an entrepreneur mentorship program.
The institutional page lists a bio-incubation facility supporting entrepreneurship and innovation.
The institutional navigation lists the Discovery to Innovation Accelerator.
The institutional navigation lists the DST NIDHI C-CAMP Accelerator.
The institutional navigation lists WE-Bio (Women Entrepreneurs in Biotechnology).
The institutional navigation lists a Centre of Excellence for Agri Innovation.
The institutional navigation lists MedTech Rapid Prototyping.
The institutional navigation lists Indigenous Diagnostics.
The institutional navigation lists Bio for Climate & Sustainability.

A probiotics company whose flagship product is a proprietary cholesterol reducing probiotic formulation.
Developing affordable mass-customizable silicone-based prostheses by indigenization of materials, equipment & processes.
Testing a new potentially path-breaking diagnostic technique for point-of-care diagnosis of TB.
Aims to transform how food and beverages are tested for chemicals. They have developed a high throughput method for analysis of pesticides in grapes.

: (Supported under BIRAC SEED and BIRAC LEAP): BioPrime is developing new solutions in plant breeding. Their patented technology uses agriculture biologicals to activate/regulate/modulate certain novel targets in plant or pest physiology.
Developing a portable medical-grade refrigerator for last mile delivery of vaccines, biological samples, breast milk, and other biological samples.
: Developing an affordable data-science-driven electronic platform for myoelectric prosthetic limbs.
: Focused on developing diagnostic kits for quantitative detection of biomarkers for obesity and cardiovascular diseases.
Use novel hollow fiber technology to offer cost-effective solutions for oxygen-enriched sterile air for medical applications.
: Developing biosurfactant-based products for food disinfection and preservation.
Developing a breath-based diagnostic for early stage detection of breast cancer.
Developing rapid detection methods for UTI causing pathogens and antibiotic sensitivity.
Aims to provide spectacle free high-quality vision to cataract surgery patients using a novel intra-ocular lens technology.

Involved in manufacturing of single-use bioreactors (SUB’s) for cell-culture-based bioprocessing applications i.e., vaccines and biologics production. OmniBRx provides innovative and universal bioprocessing solutions for highly efficient and scalable cell-culture-based vaccine manufacturing.
A biomedical products company with a focus on synthetic biodegradable, polymeric materials.

Developing innovative technologies for sustainable use of bioresources particularly of North East India. Presently, they are working towards developing an innovative fermentation-distillation pipeline for improved production of fragrant agarwood oil, considered the most expensive essential oil in the world.

PadCare Labs is tackling the problem of menstrual waste management.They have developed the world’s first smokeless sanitary pad disposal and recycling system, which can prevent 1500 pads a day from reaching landfills.
Developing cervical cancer screening that can be brought to every doorstep, ensuring timely detection for this preventable and curable condition.
Their microbial consortium offers cost-effective waste waster treatment and bio-methane production through Anaerobic Digestion.
Building a patent-protected platform that enables faster development of new vaccines for emerging viral diseases.
Develop and sell biomedical products based on silk fibroin. Looking for funds to conduct advanced preclinical trials and exploratory clinical investigations.
Developing a patented and first-of-its-kind integrated device to predict, monitor and treat Hypoxic Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) in new-borns.
Aims to use a proprietary proteomics-based platform to identify well-differentiated, clinically relevant, new drug targets and develop new chemical entities (NCEs).
Offers the only bedside diagnostics assay for salivary monitoring of biomarkers which can help diagnose neonatal sepsis, assess its severity, and guide antimicrobial treatment.
(Funded under BIRAC SEED and POC initiative) : Focused on R&D, manufacture, and commercialization of proprietary IP-driven bioactive glass products that aid in bone and tooth repair.
Vidcare is developing a TSH test for screening of hypothyroidism during pregnancy.

: (Funded under NSTEDB SSS) WeInnovate has developed a urinary catheter designed to reduce the incidences of Catheter-associated UTIs in patients. Their SilvoGuard antimicrobial Foley catheters are made antimicrobial using a patented NanoAgCide technology, comprising of active Colloidal Silver Nanoparticles.

Labs (Supported under the Lab2Mkt initiative) Working on sustainable solutions that can compete with conventional packaging in terms of costs, quality, function and production. They offer tailor-made lightweight bioplastic compounds and 100% biodegradable, water-soluble plastics.

Rechargion Energy is undertaking research, development and manufacture of next generation sodium-ion batterie. The company is also developing Lithium-Sulphur batteries which have a potential for 3-5 fold improved energy density over Li-ion technologies at an acceptable weight.

Utopic tech is focused on bringing world class diagnostics to the remotest parts of India. They are currently developing a revolutionary point of care device for kidney function testing, which can help diagnose and monitor kidney disease quickly through a finger prick sample.

Fastsense is developing a portable, easily usable device to provide rapid results at affordable cost. Using just a drop of blood, their diagnostic device is expected to identify the stage of cancer, the possibility of cancer onset and monitor patient treatment.

Divish Mobility (BatteryPool) is driving the adoption of electric 2 wheelers by offering Battery Swapping as a charging solution for EV fleets. The swap stations can be customized and BatteryPool swap station functionalities are accessible via easy-to-use APIs that can integrate with in-house fleet/ operations applications.

The company intends to transform the physical rehabilitation and fitness sector by developing robotic assistive technologies. It is developing an intelligent lower limb robotic device that learns & takes over all the repetitive exercises performed by a physiotherapist on a patient.

JyoSH AI is developing an Integrated Agriculture Robot™ which is expected to automate cotton crop cultivation activities like seed sowing, weed detection and removal, crop monitoring and cotton picking, by leveraging Artificial Intelligence, machine learning and robotics.

Neuphony is developing an EEG head band which is expected to sense the brain wave pattern and transmit it to a mobile app. After connecting the device and attaching the sensors properly, the application creates a brain map.

Denovo is a clinician led, deep-tech, R&D-driven surgical instrument startup currently focused on solutions for minimally invasive surgeries. The vision of the startup is to empower surgeons with advanced surgical instruments to deliver exceptional outcomes for patients.

Wissenkraft Labs is developing Ha and Ti coatings for bone implants. These are novel orthopedic implant coating to eliminate the risk of early revision surgeries. Wissenkraft develops and offers innovative surface coating products for biomedical industry. Presently, the company emphasizes on developing & commercializing specialized coating to enhance the functional performance of orthopedic joint replacement implants

Neuranics Labs is developing diagnostic medical devices initially focused on providing a quick CBC test using microfluidic kit, point of care blood analyzer and AI assistance. This is intended to provide a visual reporting system for blood in 10 minutes.

EyeROV is a marine robotics startup that is developing underwater drones/remotely-operated vehicles for defence, research, and disaster management organisations and also provides underwater inspection services using underwater robots/ROV to dams, bridges, oil and gas, ports and shipping sectors.

Anatomech is India’s 1st and among the world’s top 5 to extend Wearable Technology beyond monitoring and sensing. They make smart bionic technology for wearable devices to manage Chronic swelling and pain in the limbs due to underlying health conditions and also for sports rehabilitation by applying healthy pre-calibrated pressures to the limbs. Their pilot product is a medical device for Lymphedema, a chronic swelling accompanied with excruciating pain, affecting cancer survivors.

Intignus Biotech is developing simple and accessible solutions in the area of maternal and child health care. They have developed a test platform with a rapid turnaround time, low cost, minimal infrastructure and manpower – suited for use anywhere. Their first product is focused on addressing the unmet need of early diagnosis of pregnancy-related disorders, specifically preeclampsia and premature labour – which are the two major issues expecting mothers and their unborn children encounter.

Aamikza Biotechnology addresses the bacteriophage problem in fermented milk products like Dahi/curd, Cheese, Lassi, Buttermilk on ongoing batch production faced by the Dairy industry in India. The company is set to have bacteriophage resistant dairy starter cultures which can gives consistent quality without culture rotation. Due to lack of robust and affordable technology availability, India do not have competitive culture manufacturers.

Hydrovert is working on solutions in the area of clean energy that will offer a sustainable and efficient alternative to traditional fossil fuel-powered solutions. They are developing hydrogen powered drive trains ideal for use in 2 wheelers, 3 wheelers, boats and for stationary power generation.
The company is working on a patented intra-oral device for patients suffering from obstructive sleep apnea.
The company is working to solve the water, food, soil and air contamination caused by waste dry cell batteries. The startup is working on dry cell recycling and metal extraction technology.

Accensible Solutions is building “Digital Rehabilitation Platform”, a cloud-based solution that leverages a large repository of auditory stimulus. It empowers Audiologists and Special Educators to create highly customized end-to-end rehabilitation & training programs as per the patient’s varying hearing evaluation, diagnostic outcomes, demographic needs (language, age, context, etc.) and their response to the program.

Odisha policy framework to create a startup hub, encourage sector-specific incubators, support at least 5,000 startups over five years, and institutionalise implementation through a Startup Council, Task Force, and Startup Secretariat at O-Hub.
Recognised eligible startup may receive monthly payment, initially directly and subsequently against utilisation reporting; benefit can be availed once for one year.
Recognised startup submits a self-contained product-development plan online; approved amount may be released 50% in advance and 50% after utilisation evidence.
Recognised startup submits a self-contained plan explaining need and utilisation; payment may be made directly after approval and utilisation documents are required.
Recognised startups may avail subsidised incubation space in government incubators recognised under Startup Odisha.
Recognised startups representing Odisha may receive economy-class airfare or 3-tier AC train fare and free stall space at reputed national/international events, subject to policy conditions.
Approved aspiring/existing incubators submit online monetary-grant application and documents; disbursal may follow approved budget/utilisation plan and funds brought in.
Approved existing incubator may claim utility expenses with bills and utilisation certificate.
Approved incubator submits a list of successful incubatees incubated for at least three months; one-time payment may be made after approval.
O-Hub is the Startup Odisha implementation and incubation hub at Chandaka, Bhubaneswar, and hosts the Startup Secretariat route.

The Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University (GGSIPU), New Delhi, has established the Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) under the auspices of the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog, Govt. of India. The AIC has been registered as a Section 8 company under the aegis of GGSIPU and is known as the AIC GGSIPU Foundation Delhi. AIC GGSIPU is a sector-agnostic, technology-focused business incubator. However, certain domains, as mentioned below, are preferred to enable a larger societal impact: Health-Tech, Env-Tech, Agri-Tech, and Social-Tech The R&D facilities and services of the Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University-partnered institutions are also available to support the activities of the startups. The incubation centre is developing and undertaking training programmes for startups in the relevant areas, including product conceptualization, design and development, regulatory matters, technology and business strategy development, networking and partnership nurturing, attracting investors for fundraising, intellectual property, marketing, contract development, and more.

AIC@36Inc has set up a 32,273 sq.ft. working space in Raipur, the capital city of Chhattisgarh. It is developed with a seating capacity for more than 150 individuals. Also, the space homes various meeting & conference rooms along with an auditorium, cafeteria & other facilities. To guide startups, workshops on various business aspects are conducted. Also, 36Inc has partnered with a few educational institutes, independent bodies like Headstart Foundation & state government departments like CSIDC, CHiPS, Dept. of E&IT (CG). This motivates startups to network among enthusiastic brains.

AIC-Aartech is one of the first corporate Atal Incubation Centres being established under the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), a flagship initiative of NITI AAYOG, Government of India. Backed by the host institution, M/s Aartech Solonics Limited – a 30+ year old enterprise working in the field of selected and specialized energy. The incubation centre is setup in the industrial area of Mandideep, District Raisen, Madhya Pradesh – about 20 kms from Bhopal,Madhya Pradesh. A 10,000+ sqft area within Aartech’s premises have been earmarked and developed to create a unique startup incubator thriving in an industrial environment and inspired by the innumerable MSME’s that serve as the backbone to the country’s development and organized employment of its human resources. Their objective is to set up and implement the Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) in partnership with Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog with an objective of supporting innovative technology based startup enterprises in India.

AIC-AAU Incubator popularly known as North East Agriculture Technology Entrepreneurs Hub (NEATEHUB) is an “Atal Incubation Centre” of NITI Aayog, Government of India. It has been set up as a Section 8 Company under the aegis of Assam Agricultural University, Jorhat, Assam to build successful startups in the area of agriculture and allied agriculture . NEATEHUB is also ‘Knowledge Partner under the RKVY-RAFTAAR scheme’ by the Department of Agri Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Govt. of India. The Incubator has elements such as physical space, lab provisions, network activities, partnerships and linkages – both institutional and individual, mentors and advisors – to enable startups to structure their business and make them “investment-ready” to potential investors. NEATEHUB ‘Incubation Program’ aims to identify young entrepreneurs at various stages of their development (ideation/ prototype development/ early stage to growth stage) and provide the much-needed mentoring support and industry exposure to facilitate them to develop a viable business proposition. So far, NEATEHUB has successfully completed 5 Cohorts with a total of around 83 incubatees in the pre seed and seed stage from various realm of agri and allied sectors such as Digital Agriculture, Food Processing, SCM, Biotechnology, Farm Mechanization, Agri to waste management, FAAS, Protected Cultivation, Quality Input, Bamboo Craft, Bioflocs, Agro Tourism etc. With a mission to promote entrepreneurial spirit of the region, NEATEHUB has been organizing various sensitization workshops and handholding agri incubators in North eastern region. The centre has collaborated with various academic institutions and corporates to strengthen the entrepreneurial ecosystem of the region.

Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) set up with name AIC-ADT Baramati Foundation at Agricultural Development Trust Baramati with the support of Atal Innovation Mission NITI Aayog with the aim of serving as an active catalyst for the development of promising entrepreneurs. AIC-ADT focuses on supporting Start-ups in the domains: Agriculture, Healthcare & Pharma, Information Technology, Manufacturing & Engineering, Other Area of Social and National Interest. AIC-ADT Baramati Foundation has FabLab & Makers Space, Food & Agri Innovation Lab, Food, Pharma & Agri Analysis Facility with Co-working Spaces.

AIC AUDF is a not for profit Sec (8) company supported by AIM, NITI AAYOG. The main focus of this AIC is to support early stage enterprises (ideation/PoC etc) with an innovation in product or services creating a measurable impact. These startups would be provided with funding access, capacity building/knowledge sharing workshops, mentoring, market linkages and other common services. Being a part of Ambedkar University, Delhi, it is strategically positioned in terms of its academic network and will be leveraging those pool and also Industry 4.0 lab facilities.

Sector specific incubator focussed only on health technology and allied disciplines. A part of the manufacturing ecosystem in Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone. Interest areas are scalable technologies and Technology Readiness Level bridging innovations.

AIC Anna University Incubation Foundation is a section 8 company founded by the Anna University with the grant from Atal Innovation Mission, Government of India to build a vibrant innovation and startup ecosystem and also to provide innovation, incubation and startup services to budding entrepreneurs. Anna University has its strength of technocrats and innovation system with synergy of expertise in frontal areas of Science, Technology and Engineering.

The centre will play crucial role in hand holding of bright ideas from students, lecturers, professors, researchers, grass root innovators as well as individuals from Marathwada region to create competitive, market ready and sustainable start-ups and business of tomorrow. Through it’s state of the art infrastructure, University Research Centres, Forthcoming prototyping labs, Panel of eminent mentors from Industry & Academia centre will de risk the incubatee start-ups to enhance their chance to succeed. It will enable entrepreneurs to seek seed and growth capital from various government, non-government funding agencies, HNI’s, Angel investors and Venture Capital Firms. We will help entrepreneurs to identify potential of in their innovation, protect them under IPR law framework and provide access to markets. We are working towards creation of world class start up ecosystem right here in Aurangabad.

Banasthali Vidyapith, 'the world’s largest residential university for women' has established a world class Atal Incubation Centre (AIC). AIC is one of its kind Business Incubator in India solely focusing on women-led startups providing 360° support, world class infrastructure and a conducive environment for women startups to grow. The AIC with the vision to build “National Centre for Women Entrepreneurship” offers highly customized solutions, huge industry network, operating facilities and access to funding. Programs at AIC are also supported by the Ministry of MSME, MeitY and Corporates.

AIC- BIMTECH is a sector agnostic business incubator. It supports all selected startups to become successful enterprises through sector-wise expert mentoring and coaching. It has 31 mentors & 61 partnerships. These 61 partnerships give a benefit of INR 8.5 Cr. (Approx 1.2 Mn USD) to each incubatee. The incubator also has an extensive network of domestic and international investors. It has 3 programs- Khoj (Ideation to Prototype), Gurukul (First Level Revenue Generation) and Udaan (Acceleration). Startups can apply in the category that best suits them. <www.aicbimtech.com>

AIC- BV Foundation is registered as a company under Section 8 of Companies Act 1956. It has been established by Bihar Vidyapith with support from Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog, Government of India . Objectives: • To Promote Commerce and Industry in state of Bihar • To Promote Entrepreneurship & Startup • To establish World Class Incubation Facilities including physical,Lab,co-sharing,Financial and patent Right. • To Provide support to start ups or Innovators in core sectors of economy • To encourage Creation of New Technologies and Intellectual Property.
Catalyst AIC is an inclusive tech incubator, with a mission to support entrepreneurs developing technology products for the rural and semi-urban India.

"The Coffee Board of India in its continuous endeavour to encourage entrepreneurship in the coffee sector has established an Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) by enabling the collaboration between Central Coffee Research Institute (CCRI - a Nationally Important research institute established in 1929, working under administrative control of the Coffee Board) and Atal Innovation Mission (AIM). The incubation centre is called the AIC – CCRI - Centre for Entrepreneurship Development (CED). AIC CCRI CED will create an entrepreneur friendly eco-system for encouraging business innovations in coffee sector. It is envisioned that AIC – CCRI – CED will successfully incubate & graduate a minimum of 100 coffee based startups in the next 5 years. AIC CCRI CED has initiated the incubation process and has also started an intensive Pre – Incubation program named ‘Varttarambha – Let’s Enterprise’ to provide valid coffee sectoral & business knowledge for entrepreneurs for creating a realistic business idea which can be incubated into a commercial success The AIC – CCRI - CED is located in Coffee Board’s head office in Bengaluru. The incubation centre will have all the facilities and mentorship support required for the entrepreneurs to develop their business idea in to a commercial success."

AIC-CCMB is an incubator dedicated to providing a thriving ecosystem for start-ups and scientists with early stage technologies in life sciences through funding opportunities, latest equipment, mentorships and financial advice. We aim to transform scientific research into successful start-ups that can help alleviate the quality of life of the general population and mitigate some of the world’s biggest challenges in healthcare, food and animal care. We endeavor to enable Indian innovators to expand the boundaries of science and help translate technologies into sustainable business solutions. <http://aic.ccmb.res.in/>

CODISSIA Defence Innovation and Atal Incubation Centre is a non-profit company established in 2019 by CODISSIA, in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. It is supported by Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog and Ministry of Defence, Government of India. CDIIC extends support to start-ups in terms of incubation of their ideas through mentors and institutions and successful graduation. CDIIC will bring value addition to partner industries / Defence Agencies by providing professional platform for design services, infrastructure support, mentoring and business/defence networking. <www.cdiic.in>

AIC C.V. Raman College of Engineering Foundation is an incubator focused on promoting entrepreneurship in technology-based solutions by start-ups and innovators.Under this program, we support our incubated start-ups with facilities like initial brainstorming, furnishing ideas, consultancy, mentorship, networking, connecting to other subject matter experts, leading them to market access, in case if they get eligible, also connect/support with funds.Focus areas are ICT, Agritech, Renewable Energy and Manufacturing, ICT. <http://aic-cgu.org.in>

Dayanand Sagar University in association with Atal Innovation Mission and NITI Aayog has established the Atal Incubation Centre-Dayanand Sagar University (AIC-DSU) Foundation in Bengaluru. The AIC-DSU is primarily established to bring in a problem-solving culture as well as to foster world-class innovation-incubation models. This culture coupled with the ecosystem that is supportive of innovation would enable ideas to flourish. Good and promising ideas are taken up for further nurturing and examined for its business potential. <https://dsu.edu.in/innovation-labs>

"This unique incubation facility is built around the uniqueness that incubation and acceleration does not happen in isolation of individual entrepreneurial ideas, but an active incubation system that works simultaneously with multiple stakeholders in an ecosystem format to create High Impact Scalable Projects with strong marketable traction. This incubation facility aims to provide uniqueness that includes: • Co-working space located in a clean and green environment with a possibility for hostel facility if required • Fab Lab, Hardware in the Loop Simulation Lab, Advanced Design and Simulation Studio, Artificial Intelligence Lab and Bot Lab with state-of-the-art Infrastructure where start-ups can design their dream products, systems and solutions • Live Labs with possibility to actually field test the prototypes • In-house mentoring • Specific specialized mentoring by connecting with our strong network of national and international mentors and partners • Training workshops and interactive sessions to address skill gaps and get advice on how to address roadblocks with a practical approach • Events and one-on-one sessions to pitch ideas, products and solutions for fund raising • Connect with start-ups, incubators, experts, VCs, in India and worldwide through our eco-system linkages " <https://aic-empi.org>

Social Alpha is an initiative to strengthen the science and technology start-up ecosystem in India with a focus on “lab to market” enablement. Since its inception in 2016, Social Alpha has nurtured more than 130 mission driven start-ups. Social Alpha architecture integrates the innovation, incubation and investment ecosystems and allows for an effective mechanism for allocating resources to mission driven entrepreneurs throughout their lab to market progression. <https://www.socialalpha.org>

"Atal Incubation Centre, Goa Institute of Management (AICGIM) has been set up by Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) under NITI Aayog. With the mission to aid startups, stimulate their growth and facilitate their success through a holistic support system for entrepreneurs by providing them opportunities to access mentors who are industry experts, investment support, access to the startup ecosystem of India, access to flagships events and networking opportunities with growing startup ecosystems. AIC GIM is sector agnostic and also works with startups at all stages.There are 4 programs throughout the year and headway is the flagship program to guide startups in reaching the required investment." <https://www.aicgim.in/>

Atal Incubation Center at Gujarat Technological University (AIC-GISC Foundation) supported by Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog aims to facilitate technology-based start-ups with focus on Bio-Medical Devices, Biotechnology & ICT Health. The incubator strives to nurture ideas to viable enterprises. The incubator intends to setup incubation facilities with necessary infrastructure & resources supporting Technology based start-ups. <www.aic-gisc.gtu.ac.in>

AGBI envisions fostering disruptive innovation in the domains of Financial Technology, Educational Technology, Health Technology, Agricultural Technology and Energy/Ecology Technology. It would encourage nascent entrepreneur to leverage emerging technologies such as Augmented/Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, Machine Learning, Algorithmic Analytics and Blockchain to lead platform-revolution and inclusive enterprises. <http://agbinc.in/>

AIC GUSEC Foundation is a non profit company promoted by Gujarat University and setup with support from Atal Innovation Mission - NITI Aayog, Govt. of India. The company is established with a vision to be a global support system for innovators, entrepreneurs, and startups creating an impact in the society through innovation. <www.aicgusec.org>

The incubation centre, AIC IIITKottayam Foundation, is a non-profit Sec.8 company, hosted by Indian Institute of Information Technology Kottayam. It is sanctioned under the Atal Innovation Mission scheme of Govt. of India. The centre will address the existing problems of entrepreneurs by providing them sufficient input in terms of knowledge, guidance, mentoring, training, and demonstrations. The centre will incubate customers to increase the utility of technology relating to IoT and Cloud solutions for societal benefits. <http://icentre.iiitkottayam.ac.in>

AIC-IIITH FOUNDATION was set up by International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad for exclusively incubating and supporting tech-based social enterprises. AIC-IIITH seeks to deploy the entrepreneurial energy and catalyse technological innovation for social impact to help India achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). <https://aic.iiit.ac.in/>

The vision for AIC\_IISER Pune is to stimulate the growth of technology-based start-up companies and other compatible businesses in the domains of Artificial Intelligence and Data Analysis, Biotechnology and Healthcare, Energy, and Material Sciences. The total available area of 10,000 sqft that is dedicated for this AIC includes customizable lab space, office space as well as common areas such as instrumentation room and conference hall. We plan to incubate startups from within IISER Pune as well as outside.

"The Atal Incubation Centre IIT Delhi Sonipat Innovation Foundation a Section 8 company created by FITT and IIT Delhi at the I-TEC, IIT Delhi Sonipat Campus under the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) of the NITI AAYOG. AIM is supporting the AIC for creating world-class incubation facility with over 10,000 sqft of space and state-of- the-art physical infrastructure, in terms of capital equipment and operating facilities for incubatee start- ups. Apart from this, business-planning support, access to sectoral experts for mentoring and seed capital, industry partnerships, training and other relevant components required for supporting innovative start- ups will be provided." <https://fitt-iitd.in/atal-incubation-centre-aic-iit-delhi-sonipat-innovation-foundation/>

AIC ISB Association is the incubation and acceleration arm of the Indian School of Business, set up in partnership with Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog. The objective of AIC ISB is to nurture innovative startups by guiding them to become scalable and sustainable enterprises. The business-driven incubator supports selected startups at the Proof-of-Concept stage and beyond by providing state-of-the-art resources and leveraging ISB’s core strengths. <https://aicisb.org/>

The foundation provides an ecosystem to facilitate and promote entrepreneurship in areas of chemical synthesis, medicinal chemistry, nano-chemistry, green chemistry, healthcare, biotechnology, pharmaceutical sciences and IoT. <www.aicisefoundation.org>

"The AIC-JNUFI is formed to promote and support start-ups in various sectors like health, IT, energy/environment, food/agriculture, rural technologies, and other areas, without limiting the scope of activities. The major ideas the AIC-JNUFI is considering in its working are: 1\. To scout innovations available in a rural and urban setup 2\. To develop research and innovation e-network 3\. To promote interdisciplinary research with the involvement of all the available research capabilities of the university 4\. To contribute to the promotion of the innovation mandate of the university 5\. To develop knowledge capacity for promoting entrepreneurship 6\. To develop technology and knowledge transfer principles from academia to industry and vice-versa. 7\. To promote active academia-industry research collaborations"

AIC-JKLU is an Atal Incubation Center established by Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog, Government of India. It is promoted by JK Laxhmipat University, the university Supported by the 125 years old legacy of contributions to nation-building by the JK Organization.AIC-JKLU's vision is to develop an incubation center that fosters the dynamic needs of the entrepreneurs not only in Rajasthan but across India through its virtual incubation programs. The focus of the AIC-JKLU is to support all the startups of all stages and across all sectors and stages. <http://www.aicjklu.in/>

Under the aegis of NITI Aayog, GoI, the Atal Incubation Centre – Jyothy Institute of Technology Foundation (AIC-JITF) opens a plethora of opportunities for budding entrepreneurs who dream of establishing a strong foothold in the entrepreneurial world. AIC-JITF housed within JIT campus. AIC-JITF leverages facilities such as laboratories, testing centre, highly experienced and knowledgeable human resource available through the state of the art R&D centre – CIIRC which is an integral part of the institute. AIC-JITF focuses on Materials, Food Technology, Devices and Sensors. <https://aicjitf.org/>

"AIC-LMCP Foundation is a non-profit incubator hosted by L.M. College of Pharmacy, Ahmedabad and supported by AIM, NITI Aayog, Govt. of India. It focuses on fostering entrepreneurship in the Pharmaceutical and Healthcare sector (including food, nutrition, devices, diagnostics, patient care, AYUSH and related fields). It offers state-of-art laboratory facilities, workspaces, rich domain expertise, support for IP, legal, business strategy, marketing, regulatory and mentorship, collaboration and networking with leading industry/ecosystem, investment and funding facilitation, for the innovators." <http://aiclmcp.org/>

Atal Incubation Centre in the name of AIC Mahamana Foundation for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (AIC-MFIE-IM-BHU) is now on operation at Institute of Management, Banaras Hindu University inaugurated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji in September 2018. Atal Innovation Mission is an initiative started by the NITI Aayog, Government of India, expressing its pledge to the vision of Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ji, of a modern innovative India, committed to the economic progress and social well-being of every citizen across the length and breadth of the country and across all walks of life. AIM intends to form centres called Atal Incubation Centres (AICs) that would nurture innovative start-up businesses in their pursuit to become scalable and sustainable enterprises. The purpose of AIC-MFIE-IM-BHU is to stimulate the growth of innovation-based ideas into reality through their support, a proper channelized entry in a competitive environment and by multidisciplinary exposure, and these setups help indirectly in job creation within the region to start with and can scale-up in near future.

It is one of the first Institution supported by AIM, NITI Aayog, Govt. of India at any private university across Maharashtra.It's main objective is to build the ecosystem of Entrepreneurship. AIC-MIT ADT will incubate the potential founders and support them by building a 'Learning Culture'. It aims to build a community that nurtures the IDEA (Innovation, Design Thinking, Entrepreneurship, Arts) among the Next Generation of Entrepreneurs.

AIC-MUJ aims to support and encourage innovative technology enabled startups that have application and/or impact in the core sectors of the startups with necessary guidance, tech support infrastructure, access to investors, networking, and facilitating a host of other resources that may be required for the startup to survive and scale.

AIC-Nalanda Institute of Technology Foundation is a Technology Business Incubator supported by Atal Innovation Mission, a flagship initiative set up by the NITI Aayog, Government of India to promote innovation and entrepreneurship across the nation. Our Incubation Centre is headed by experienced professionals who converge their experience and expertise of respective fields to guide and mentor the young aspiring minds to realize their ideas and scale up their business.

The AIC NCore Developmental Impact Foundation is a nonprofit organisation working towards poverty alleviation in India. Focused on solving societal and developmental challenges in India, the foundation works on problems that mainly addresses health, education, employment, sanitation and sustainability, that aims at improving the quality of life for the economically disadvantaged. Along with support for various programs, the foundation also aims at improving the capacity of the nonprofit sector to attract talent in legal aid, media, impact studies, data and research.

The AIC NITTE Incubation Centre is situated amidst the luscious green fields of Nitte, Karlala, India. The NITTE Education Trust is one among the few reputed Institutions selected by NITI Aayog for setting up an Atal Incubation Centre sprawling across 10,000 sq ft, the Incubation Centre aims to accelerate entrepreneurial vision of the country by encouraging and providing assistance to budding entrepreneurs who want to create startups in the areas of Agriculture, Biotechnology and ITCs to nurture their Novel innovative ideas. The main objective of AIC Nitte is to foster innovation and entrepreneurship among young men and women. AIC Nitte Incubation Centre offers the start-ups with valuable guidance, technological assistance , and access to investors, networking, and facilitating a host of other services. Start-ups also receive direction through the robust chain of Mentors who give sector-specific information and real-time practical guidance. Further, the Centre will also support the existing MSMEs in the region through appropriate intervention strategies like training, consultancy/mentoring, business development, diversification, technology transfer & up-gradation. The Centre would network with industry associations and trade bodies to identify research, training, education, consulting and development needs of the MSME sector.

"AIC NMIMS Incubation Centre is launched by NMIMS (Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies) in collaboration with the Atal Innovation Mission (NITI Aayog, Government of India). It is sector agnostic Incubator established in the heart of Mumbai to provide budding entrepreneurs the ecosystem to create successful and sustainable businesses."

AIC-Pinnacle Entrepreneurship forum is a Not-for-profit, section 8 entity supported by Atal innovation Mission, NITI Aayog, Govt. of India and the industry stakeholders to facilitate employment generation, innovation creation and startup promotion. We are focused on incubating, accelerating, and funding complex, deep-technology driven, product-oriented startups. We aim to support the creation of a vibrant and high impact entrepreneurial ecosystem focused on innovation in key sectors which lead to inclusive and sustainable techno-socio-economic development of India

"Atal Incubation Centre - Pondicherry Engineering College Foundation (AIC-PECF) was initiated to provide a platform to assist and enable young entrepreneurs to initiate startups for the commercial exploitation of technologies developed by them. (AIC-PECF) is fully supported and funded by Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), Niti Aayog, Government of India. Our Focus Area includes Electronics design and Manufacturing (EDM), Internet of Things(IoT) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). AIC-PECF empowers innovators to pursue their entrepreneurial goals."

AIC- Prestige Inspire Foundation, Indore works with solemn objective of supporting innovative start-ups and enterprises. We inspire innovators to SPIRE Nurturing start-ups to become viable business ventures, thereby supporting socio-economic development of the nation. Provide overall ecosystem support to business ideas that are innovative, scaleable and sustainable with potential to disrupt business and revenue models.

AIC RAISE is India's first Startup Incubation Centre focusing on nurturing and supporting startups and entrepreneurs working around the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. AIC RAISE is creating a holistic ecosystem for social impact start-ups for maximizing profits while maximizing benefits to society and the environment. AIC RAISE is working towards the goal of bringing up 150+ successful startups over the period of next 5 years for creating a tremendous impact in the society and economy and to evolve us an international platform for social startups.

Atal Incubation Centre- Rambhau Mhalgi Prabodhini (RMP) Foundation has been set up in alignment with Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog to nurture, handhold and support New Age Entrepreneurs for New India. The focus is on job creation through entrepreneurship in the domains of Agriculture, Education & ICT. It also aims to create & support sustainable business models at grassroot level including social enterprises.

Our objective is to create a startup ecosystem and familiarize the visionary brains with the business aspects of an idea and provide them a platform with necessary resources, culture & opportunities– to grow their startup units into high growth business enterprises. We by playing the role of both startup incubator and accelerator, aims at training and mentoring young entrepreneurs to fuel their inner drive to innovate. At AIC-RNTU, we aim to provide essential services such as fund support, management, mentorship, co-working space, and state-of-the-art assistance to the budding startups.

AIC-Sangam is India’s first and only incubator dedicated to fight climate change. It is set up as a platform to bring together the best minds, resources and capital solving sustainability problems, and serve as a launch pad for inclusive and scalable enterprises focused on improving access to energy and resource productivity for the underserved in India, that will lead the way in driving inclusive development and creation of communities that are resilient to climate change.

AIC-SELCO Foundation is based out of Guwahati, Assam and aims to support and encourage start-ups in sustainable energy sector in North Eastern States and would provide them with necessary infrastructure facilities and other value-added services in . The center focuses on underserved and unserved areas to support inclusive growth. Activities and support systems available at the center include - technology development, financial modeling, business and dissemination planning, different types and stages of capital support, social and environmental evaluations.

AIC-Shiksha Infotech Foundation incubation center aims to provide early stage startups necessary support to shape their ideas into viable business with positive social impact. Our incubation center provides working space, access to industry mentors, and provides access to vibration Indian Startup EcoSystem.

Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) set up at Shiv Nadar University with the support of Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog, to serve as an active catalyst to assist budding entrepreneurs and innovators in their entrepreneurial journey. AIC is sector agnostic and welcomes start-ups from diverse fields. AIC, as a business incubator, is highly flexible and has a unique combination of business development processes, infrastructure and people designed to nurture new and small businesses by helping them to survive and grow through the difficult and vulnerable early stages of development.

AIC-SMUTBI incubates and nurtures early-stage entrepreneurial ventures from North East India at large and Sikkim in Particular. The center has persistently encouraged young entrepreneurs to hone their skills in generating Valued Human Resources rather than the traditional Man Power that feeds the needs of the industry. . Currently the incubator has 14 startups as its incubatees. This incubator envisions to work as a level playing field for startups from the North East India at par with the other parts of the country. It also is working toward employment generation through entrepreneurship.

The National Dairy Research Institute as the premier Dairy Research Institution undertakes research, teaching and extension activities towards dairy development in the country. Being the National Institute, it conducts basic and applied research with the objective to enhance animal productivity and also to develop cost effective technologies for the benefit of the teeming millions. Further, the Institute provides high quality manpower to meet the human resource requirements for the overall dairy development in the country. The Institute also undertakes extension programmes for transferring the know-how from the laboratory to the farmers’ fields.

AIC STPINEXT INITIATIVES intends to create an eco-system to nurture innovative start-up businesses in their pursuit to become scalable and sustainable enterprises under the Atal Incubation Mission. AIC STPINEXT INITIATIVES would focus on providing world class incubation facilities with suitable physical infrastructure in terms of capital equipment and operating facilities, coupled with sectoral experts for mentoring the start-ups, business planning support, access to seed capital, industry partners, trainings etc, to the innovative start-ups with a focus on healthcare, IoT, e-Commerce and ICT.

AIC SURATi iLAB Foundation is the wholly owned subsidiary of Surat Smart City Development Limited. It is a Section 8 Company Incorporated on 6th April 2018 to promote culture of Innovation ,Start up ,Incubation , Trade Facilitation &Skill Development for aspiring entrepreneurs of Surat City.

AIC T-Hub Foundation is hosted by T-Hub Foundation Hyderabad. T-Hub fosters a culture of Innovation. It leads India’s pioneering innovation ecosystem that powers next-generation products and new business models. Since its incorporation in 2015, it has provided 1,100+ national and international startups access to better technology, talent, mentors, customers, corporations, investors and government agencies. At AIC-T-Hub, sanctioned under the Atal Innovation Mission scheme of Govt. of India, we support and encourage deep tech enabled startups that have application and/or impact in the healthcare/life sciences and urban mobility sectors by creating a strong ecosystem which gives startups access to investors, mentors, industry experts, service providers and fellow entrepreneurs. We focus on startups that have past product validation stages and help them with their growth plans by providing support to understand the market, to assist with their business plans and to access the right resources at the right time.

The Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) at Jammu & Kashmir Entrepreneurship Development Institute (JKEDI) is aimed at fostering entrepreneurship providing all kinds of support related to mentoring, counseling, technical support, shared facilities and any other business services that are desired for their success so that they can accelerate at a faster pace and create adequate revenue and jobs for others in the entire region of Kashmir. The AIC is setup in the established premises of JKEDI which is centrally located in Kashmir. The AIC is a ‘Mixed Use’ Incubator i.e., it will enroll incubatees who ...
Official AIM selected AIC profile listing this incubator and its public support focus.

India's marginalized producers battle formidable odds to eke out a fragile livelihood. Established in 2005, Access Livelihoods Consulting India (ALC India) is a social enterprise that partners with more than 65,000 marginalized producers, including small and marginal farmers, weavers, tribals, and small livestock holders. To such producers, ALC India offers professional services that they can use to turn the odds in their favour and build livelihoods that are more certain, rewarding, and sustainable. As part of this effort, ALC India incubates enterprises that the communities own, typically cooperatives or producer companies and develops producers’ technical, managerial, and entrepreneuri...

The Amity Innovation Incubator is a pioneering concept in the context of Indian Universities. Amity Technology Incubator (Amity Innovation Incubator) was established in 2007 with a vision to promote and strengthen the entrepreneurship ecosystem across the nation. www.amity.edu/aii

Amrita TBI is a non-profit startup incubator supported by Govt. of India and Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham that funds, mentors and nurtures ideas, startups and entrepreneurs. Amrita TBI runs multiple programs including Scaled Incubator program, Amrita TBI Accelerator program, Amrita TBI PitchFest and Amrita TBI StartupHub. It has built a strong network of world-class mentors and partners such as SAP Startup Studio, TATA Communications, Indian Angel Network, VenturEast, International Accelerator etc. to help startups scale nationally and internationally. Discounted services from multiple partners, GST exemption of upto Rs. 50 Lakhs per year for a period of 3 years are other benefits provided ...

"ALEAP a Sec 25 (Sec 8) Company reg. under Companies Act, 1956, has completed 25 yrs of committed service, as a facilitator to help women to become economically independent. AIC ALEAP We-Hub, ALEAP’s manufacturing multisector business incubator for innovative startups is supported by AIM, NITI Aayog, GoI. It provides services like co-working spaces; lab, machinery & market support; mentorship; seed funding, facilitation to Banks & VCs; along with accelerator eco system. Focus Areas: Food processing, Biotechnology, Biodegradable Technologies, Electronics & Engineering, 3D Printing and IT&ITES " www.aicaleapwehub.in

Centre for Cellular And Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP) is an initiative of Dept of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science and Technology, Govt. of India, with a mandate to be an enabler of cutting edge Life Science Research and Innovation. Bio-incubator at C-CAMP has in the last few years emerged as a thriving hub for innovation with a vibrant ecosystem. It has interacted with over 500 inventors and entrepreneurs and encouraged them to translate their inventions into innovation. Furthermore, C-CAMP has engaged quite extensively with entrepreneurs before and after incorporation of their ventures, through its bio-incubation and mentorship program. C-CAMP's entrepreneurial activities include provi...

Established in 2002, NSRCEL - the start-up hub at Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB), is sector agnostic and has incubated over 225 start-ups, created over 5400+ jobs and associated with roughly 46,000 entrepreneurs since its inception. NSRCEL brings together Start-ups, Industry mentors, Eminent academicians, Researchers and Alumni of IIMB to create a unique ecosystem specially tailored for early-stage ventures. With the support of Government, Corporate and Institutional partners, this centre for excellence promotes entrepreneurship with emphasis on early stage for profit ventures, businesses by women entrepreneurs and social ventures. https://www.nsrcel.org/

Society for Innovation and Development (SID) is a Society founded by IISc in 1997 to promote collaboration with the Industry. SID today is a well-known, domain agnostic, deep science incubation centre that focusses on incubating IP-based, Deep Science startups. Currently, SID has a portfolio of over 30 startups spread across various domains such as Agri-Tech, Bio-Tech, Space-Tech, Clean-Tech, Medical Devices, Life Sciences etc. Some of our past startups include the likes of Strand LifeSciences, Mymo Wireless, PathShodh Healthcare Pvt Ltd, Bellatrix Aerospace Pvt. Ltd etc. https://sid.iisc.ac.in/

91springboard is a vibrant and diversified community led incubator, committed to fostering an entrepreneurial community and support system for individuals and teams to ideate build and expand great ideas. We combine technology and innovation in a state-of-the-art workspace. We’re obsessed with assisting our startups in growing their businesses and achieve their vision. http://91springboard.com

TREC-STEP is one of the first Incubators, promoted in the country, in 1986, as a multi-stakeholder organization, by Govt. of India, Govt. of Tamil Nadu, Central & State Financial Instns. & others. It has always been a pioneering ‘Development Lab’ for piloting impactful incubation & innovation schemes, working with Govt. of India and also successfully implementing novel developmental projects with World Bank, UNOs, EU, etc. Mentored many incubators, as Founder President of Indian Science Parks & Business Incubators Asstn. as well as Honorary President of Asian Asstn. of Business Incubation. http://www.trecstep.com/index.html

The Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) at Jammu & Kashmir Entrepreneurship Development Institute (JKEDI) is aimed at fostering entrepreneurship providing all kinds of support related to mentoring, counseling, technical support, shared facilities and any other business services that are desired for their success so that they can accelerate at a faster pace and create adequate revenue and jobs for others in the entire region of Kashmir. The AIC is setup in the established premises of JKEDI which is centrally located in Kashmir. The AIC is a ‘Mixed Use’ Incubator i.e., it will enroll incubatees who plan to start their business in different sectors like agriculture and allied activities, education, manufacturing, environmental sustainability, tourism, waste management and other focus areas of social or national importance. In line with its mandate, the Institute strives to develop entrepreneurship and entrepreneurial culture through entrepreneurship education, skill up-gradation, knowledge dissemination, consultancy services and developing linkages with national and international organizations to make entrepreneurship the mainstay of the region’s economy. The Institute is committed to self-sustenance; positive, healthy and competitive work culture, teamwork, quality improvement, excellence and professionalism in all aspects of its working.

Official NSA 5.0 taxonomy card and modal description: This accolade celebrates startups founded by students who have created groundbreaking solutions at a young age. These young entrepreneurs demonstrate remarkable innovation, driving significant advancements across various fields.

The official results landing describes NSA as a flagship platform recognising exemplary startups and enablers, including innovative/scalable enterprises with potential for employment or wealth creation and measurable social impact. It publishes category navigation and an all-finalists organisation list.

The official category page publishes winner Aviotron Aerospace Private Limited and seven finalists: Tyromer Technology Private Limited, Revasa Farms Private Limited, Chimertech Private Limited, Sarvajna Edutech Private Limited, Preskilet Edtech Private Limited, Loom&Weaver Retail Private Limited and Umarobotics Technology Private Limited. It describes public company claims including STEM labs, curriculum alignment, trainers, mentorship/competitions, DIY kits and global expansion.
MAARG landing page states startups can find relevant mentors based on sector, stage and other needs.
Startup Setu describes MAARG as a single-stop solution finder accessible across India to connect startups with mentors using human intelligence.
Startup Setu states MAARG uses Artificial Intelligence for matchmaking between mentors and startups and sustains the function with Machine Learning.
Startup Setu lists online access, calendar/scheduling, custom user dashboards and mentor-hosted masterclasses/classroom sessions.
Startup Setu states the portal supports cohort-based programmes and outcome-driven activities to monitor matchmaking and mentor engagement KPIs, with query/grievance handling.

Startup Setu aims to provide mentorship and customised assistance with deal flow of high-potential Indian startups to US-based investors and ecosystem leaders; participation by mentors/industry experts is voluntary.
Official mentor dashboard exposes discovery routes for mentors, incubators, accelerators, startups and investors; it states a maximum of three connection requests per week for mentors and incubators.

Startup Setu states that MAARG’s application process is enabled at a single go and can be accessed using desktop or mobile devices, with the portal intended to connect startups from every corner of India to mentors.
Startup Setu states that MAARG accepts user queries and grievances to ensure timely issue resolution within the portal.
Startup Setu states that mentors and industry experts interested in investing in high-potential startups may express interest through a linked form to get connected to startups, on a voluntary basis.
Startup India states startups can create a GeM seller profile using DPIIT recognition number, recognition-linked mobile number, PAN and Aadhaar, then sell to government entities.
GeM Startup Runway provides a dedicated route for innovative products unique in design, process or functionality to reach government buyers.

GeM Exclusive describes Startup Runway 2.0 as a dedicated marketplace category allowing startups to list multiple products/services with minimal technical specifications across 13 recognised startup sub-sectors.

Official GeM taxonomy covers advanced manufacturing/robotics, AdTech, AgTech/new foods, AI, big data/analytics, AR/VR, blockchain, clean tech/renewables, consumer home electronics/wearables/smart devices, cybersecurity, EdTech, fintech and health/life sciences/watertech.
Startup India describes exemptions for DPIIT-recognised startups from prior experience, prior turnover and earnest money deposit requirements under applicable central procurement orders.
CPPP publishes central tenders, corrigenda and contract awards; Startup India states startups can register as preferred bidders and obtain applicable relaxations.
Startup India links the official EMD exemption notification under Rule 170(i) for DPIIT-recognised startups.
Startup India links official notifications under Rule 173(i) concerning relaxation of prior experience and turnover for DPIIT-recognised startups.

The public grievance form accepts issues including missing prior-experience/turnover/EMD exemption, startup exclusion, GeM queries, unavailable exemptions, international-norm conditions and MII Order violations.
GeM Exclusive reports 15,665 startups registered on GeM and ₹9,512.07 crore in processed Startup Runway GMV at the page’s last-update context of 9 June 2021.
Startup India lists Kerala direct procurement, department requirement/demand days and innovation-zone models through KSUM, with stated ₹5–20 lakh direct route and limited tendering above ₹100 lakh.

Startup India describes AP Innovation Society evaluation of suo moto startup proposals, annual collective selection value up to ₹50 crore and work orders up to ₹5 crore; out-of-state companies may need a development centre in AP.
Startup India describes Rajasthan’s online Challenge for Change platform with problem statements and work orders up to ₹1 crore.

Startup India records state examples: Odisha no minimum turnover/prior experience and EMD/performance-security provisions; Gujarat removal of prior experience/turnover/tender fee/EMD; Haryana turnover/experience/tender fee/EMD concessions and L1+15% matching provision; Maharashtra Startup Week proof-of-concept work orders of ₹10–15 lakh for selected startups.

Startup India lists PSU routes including HPCL Udgam, EIL vendor enlistment, MRPL innovation/incubation, HAL Make-II, NTPC startup vendor assessment, BEL startup/Make-II provisions and AAI Startup Grand Challenge.
Current Startup India procurement page states startups can create a GeM seller profile using DPIIT Recognition Number, the mobile number used for recognition, PAN Number and Aadhaar Number.

The current Startup India page describes exemptions from prior experience, prior turnover and earnest money deposits, a Startup India badge, buyer feedback, flexible product categories and face-time opportunity with 50,000+ government buyers. The buyer figure is a stated opportunity claim, not a transaction metric.

The current public procurement page exposes counters for DPIIT-recognised startups registered on GeM, startup order volume and order value, but the captured page shows zero/loading placeholders rather than verified current values.
Startup India describes CPPP as the central portal for Central Government Departments, Organisations, Autonomous Bodies and CPSEs to publish NITs, tender enquiries, contract awards and corrigenda.

The official Startup India page states startups can register on CPPP, become Preferred Bidders in public orders and receive exemptions on prior experience, prior turnover and EMD requirements; it links CPPP and bidder-enrollment guidance.

The public CPPP landing page exposes latest active tenders, active corrigenda, tender results, GeM bids, tender search, central/state routes, dashboards, analytics, GeM statistics, grievance and procurement-policy/manual sections.
National report presents framework/methodology, evaluation process, results, state/UT ecosystem evolution, capacity development and nationwide impact across reform areas.

Compendium documents state/UT initiatives across institutional support, innovation/entrepreneurship, market access, incubation/mentorship, funding, capacity building of enablers and sustainable future.

The SRF 5.0 result page describes a DPIIT capacity-building exercise evaluating States/UTs, with consideration period 1 January 2023 to 30 November 2024, 19 action points and 34 participating entities.
The fifth edition incorporates private ecosystem mapping to evaluate ecosystem growth led by private stakeholders beyond government interventions.
The fifth edition emphasises priority-sector identification and strengthening, with a dedicated incubation-infrastructure reform area and specific action points.

The Knowledge Centre documents policy/nodal-team formulation, website/API integration, awareness and HEI programmes, GeM/procurement workshops, incubator capacity development, funding-policy creation, Virtual Mentorship Series, HNI sensitisation and showcase sessions.

Startup India describes live showcase sessions for States/UTs to present ecosystem initiatives, exchange practices and connect with the central government; examples include funding, incubation, procurement and mentorship themes.

BHASKAR is described as a one-stop digital platform connecting entrepreneurs, investors, mentors, policymakers and other ecosystem players through networking, knowledge sharing, searchability and collaboration.
The landing page states users can obtain a personalised BHASKAR ID and that only users completing ID generation and complete profiles are visible/searchable in the BHASKAR network.
Public persona options include mentor, enabler, explorer, startup founder, student, individual investor and traditional business owner, for individual and organisation contexts.

BHASKAR About page describes networking with investors, mentors, experts and peers, personalised dashboard/ID, support services, profile-card visibility and faster discoverability in India and subsequently globally.
For individual and institutional investors, BHASKAR describes curated access to startups, searchability by investment criteria and collaboration with other investors/fund managers.
For students, BHASKAR describes free tools/resources focused on startup fundamentals, business planning and innovation, plus dashboard access to mentorship and potential partnerships.

The public registration page exposes nationality selection, email/mobile OTP generation and password rules; DPIIT-recognised startups can use existing Startup India login credentials to access BHASKAR ID.
BHASKAR landing page exposes a Browse Network concept, dynamic networking, profile cards and searchability after complete profile/ID conditions.
The public landing page contains a user-count/network area without an extractable numeric current user total. National Startup Day 2026 separately displays a 6,60,000+ BHASKAR-user portal claim.
